newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch bourse gears up for hectic options expiry.
newsitem.headline: Dutch bourse gears up for hectic options expiry.

text.p: Recent hectic option and share trading has led Amsterdam Exchanges (AEX) to take precautionary measures to ensure Friday's options expiry proceeds smoothly , AEX chairman George Moeller said on Thursday.
Options trading has been boosted by the booming Dutch share market, with some 850,000 open interest option contracts recorded on Wednesday afternoon, Moeller said.

The busiest expiration ever for the exchange was in January this year when 411,000 contracts were settled. The exchange estimates its maximum daily processing capacity at more than 500,000 contracts per day.
If the processing of transactions on Friday gets too far behind, the bourse may halt clearing and continue over the weekend, Moeller said.
This meant the ultimate exercise cut off time might be delayed to later than usual on Saturday or until Sunday.
Moeller said he did not expect all options with open interest to be closed ahead of the expiry.
"The index options are settled in cash, but I expect many of the open stock-options to be closed," he said.
Moeller said that between January and April of this year, there had been a 50/50 division between exercised and closed options.
The exchange has also held back the introduction of the new one-month options contracts, usually introduced on the Wednesday ahead of expiration. These will start to trade next Monday only.
Following increased interest in the market, trade volumes on the AEX in both options and shares have surged in the first half of this year, reaching record levels, Moeller said.
